prompt: In template.py implement render(template, context) for a tiny template language. A placeholder is {{ path }} (spaces around the path, and around the filter if there is one, are ignored) where path is dot-separated names (letters, digits, underscore; each name must not be empty). Lookup starts at the context dict: a segment indexes a dict by that exact string key, or, when the current value is a list and the segment is all digits, indexes the list. Any lookup that cannot be done (missing key, bad index, indexing into a non-dict non-list) raises KeyError whose argument is the full path text. A placeholder may end with |raw (for example {{ body|raw }}); no other filter exists and any other filter raises ValueError, as does a malformed path. The value is converted to text: None becomes the empty string, True and False become 'true' and 'false', anything else uses str(). Unless |raw is used, the text is HTML-escaped by replacing & < > " and ' with & < > " and ' (ampersand first so existing replacements are not escaped twice). A backslash directly before {{ (that is \{{) produces a literal {{ and what follows is ordinary text, not a placeholder; any other backslash is ordinary text. A {{ with no closing }} raises ValueError. Text outside placeholders is copied unchanged and replaced values are never re-scanned for placeholders.
